```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(multiPPI)
```

Conventional PPI fits the interaction of a seed's estimated neural signal and
psychological input, together with the adjusted seed, task effects, and run
intercepts. It estimates a regression coefficient conditional on this design;
it does not establish causal or latent neural coupling. `mppi_fit()` instead
estimates task-modulated covariance matrices, a different estimand.

## Two runs with event inputs

Onsets and durations are in seconds from the start of each run. The seed is raw
BOLD on the full acquisition grid. By default, the builder removes run baselines
and nuisance effects from the seed conditional on centered task main effects,
then deconvolves independently by run. Use `seed_adjust = "none"` only when
the raw input needs no such adjustment. It
centers each condition on its neural grid for the interaction, reconvolves with
the specified HRF, and retains task main effects. Its microtime binning and
normalization are documented in `?ppi_design`; equivalence to another package's
PPI implementation is not implied.

```{r events}
set.seed(2026)
n <- 120L
runs <- rep(c("one", "two"), each = 60)
seed <- as.numeric(stats::arima.sim(list(ar = .35), n = n))
events <- data.frame(
  onset = rep(c(4, 16, 28, 40, 52, 64, 76, 88, 100), 2),
  duration = 2,
  condition = rep(c("A", "B", "A", "B", "A", "B", "A", "B", "A"), 2),
  run = rep(c("one", "two"), each = 9)
)
design <- ppi_design(seed, events = events, TR = 2, runs = runs,
                     run_effects = "shared")
# Synthetic target data; real target data must have the same rows as the design.
Y <- matrix(rnorm(n * 3), nrow = n)
fit <- ppi_fit(Y, design, noise = "iid")
contrast <- ppi_contrast(fit, c(A = 1, B = -1))
contrast$estimate
contrast$p_value
```

A named condition contrast selects interaction columns; with separate run
columns the condition weights average equally across runs. Aliased terms remain
in the design and nonestimable contrasts return `NA`.

## Scan-grid psychological inputs

A numeric matrix explicitly means scan-grid *neural psychological inputs*, held
constant within each TR. It is not a convolved BOLD task design. Alternatively,
use `list(values = ..., grid = "neural")` for a microtime-grid matrix.

```{r psych}
psych <- cbind(A = rep(c(0, 1), length.out = n),
               B = rep(c(0, 0, 1, 1), length.out = n))
scan_design <- ppi_design(seed, psych = psych, TR = 2, runs = runs,
                          run_effects = "shared")
scan_design$provenance$psych_grid
```

## Temporal noise and censoring

`noise = "fmriAR"` estimates a common noise operator from full-model residuals.
Shared operators assume sufficiently similar target noise: a heterogeneous
simulation in the accompanying validation found inflated false positives under
shared pooling. Fit separate operators by assigning each target its own label;
this is more expensive. Estimated-noise inference is approximate.

```{r noise}
shared <- ppi_fit(Y, design, noise = "fmriAR", noise_control = list(p = 1L))
separate <- ppi_fit(Y, design, noise = "fmriAR",
                    noise_control = list(p = 1L, pooling = "parcel",
                                         parcels = seq_len(ncol(Y))))
ppi_contrast(separate, c(A = 1, B = -1))$standard_error
```

Censoring retains the original grid. Currently a censored conventional fit
supports IID errors; an AR fit with gaps is rejected because its correct
observed-data covariance has not yet been implemented.

```{r censor}
censor <- rep(FALSE, n); censor[c(15, 75)] <- TRUE
censored_design <- ppi_design(seed, events = events, TR = 2, runs = runs,
                              censor = censor, run_effects = "shared")
censored_fit <- ppi_fit(Y, censored_design, noise = "iid")
sum(censored_fit$design$keep)
```

These examples demonstrate the API rather than statistical calibration. Legacy
covariance resampling methods that lack a supported null fail closed; model
evidence in the legacy path concerns task main effects, not interaction
likelihood evidence. See `inst/validation/README.md` in the source for the
scope of reproducible checks and their limitations.
